Phoenix NWS discussion contains a convective/monsoon signal

afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 220555
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
1055 PM MST Wed Oct 21 2026

.UPDATE...06Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A strong low pressure system will support multiple rounds of 
showers and thunderstorms, some of which may be strong to severe 
through Thursday afternoon across much of central and eastern 
Arizona.

- Moderate to heavy rainfall with totals over one inch may result 
in areas of flash flooding across south-central Arizona with a focus 
on upslope, terrain areas. 

- Drier air filtering into the region by the end of the week will 
lead to more benign weather conditions during the weekend and 
through at least early next week. 

- Near normal temperatures will cool to below normal levels 
by the latter half of the week and continuing through early next 
week.  

&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Thursday/... 
A high impact weather event continues to unfold across much of 
central and eastern Arizona, as an anomalously deep low pressure 
system along the southern California coast sends multiple shortwaves 
and favorable jet forced ascent into the region intercepting a very 
moist airmass. Objective analysis indicates a plume of total column 
PWATS in excess of 1.25" focused into central Arizona with low level 
mixing ratios 8-10 g/kg, and combined with steepening midlevel lapse 
rates (~7 C/km in the H7-H5 layer) will result in MLCape values 
nearing or exceeding 1000 J/kg by this afternoon. Juxtaposed with 
these thermodynamic profiles, deep layer 0-6km shear will easily 
exceed 50kt supporting supercellular structure/splitting cells in 
more robust thunderstorm updrafts. Special 18Z KPSR sounding 
highlights an even higher instability potential should sufficient 
heating continue supporting a severe potential with large hail and 
damaging the primary threats. Interestingly, however, the latest 
HREF and REFS output is less enthusiastic regarding the spatial 
coverage of storms across lower elevations until later this evening, 
and it remains to be seen if the ingest of updated thermodynamic 
profiles changes short term model output. Nevertheless, there is 
still modest support for terrain encouraged ascent spurring rapid 
updraft development around the Phoenix metro with better confidence 
of thunderstorm clusters to the north and east of the city through 
the evening.

Confidence in thunderstorm development and coverage across south-
central Arizona grows markedly overnight through Thursday morning as 
the aforementioned California low edges inland placing the eastern 
CWA within a right rear jet entrance region providing a prolonged 
period of upper divergence and ascent. The nocturnal tendency will 
be for increasing H9-H8 southerly winds, and within a unidirectional 
wind profile, reduce Corfidi vectors encouraging training echoes. 
Moist orographic upslope will also aid in persistent ascent over the 
same areas, and with PWATS solidly holding or exceeding 1.50" 
overnight, the flash flood threat will be heightened heading into 
Thursday morning. A notable handful of high resolution models 
support a conceptual idea and historical precedent in similar 
scenarios of storms aligned through northern Maricopa County through 
the morning hours before shifting into Gila County during the 
afternoon. The magnitude of elevated instability combined with 
abundant moisture profiles will yield a favorable environment for 
rainfall rates in excess of 1-2"/hr.

As the upper trough lifts inland towards the Great Basin Thursday, 
supporting jet energy will exit the region while low level winds 
veer helping erode boundary layer moisture, driving a frontal 
boundary and lower theta-e airmass into lower elevations and 
eliminating instability. However, moist upslope will persist across 
the eastern CWA with lingering instability juxtaposed with strong 
deep layer shear supporting the continued threat for severe weather. 
In fact, numerous HREF and REFS members depict very impressive 2-5km 
updraft helicity signatures with notable 0-1km shear indicative of 
rotating updrafts in the stronger storms through the afternoon. 
Subjectively, the synoptic setup and model output looks more 
impressive for portions of southern Gila County tomorrow than much 
of the forecast area currently. Thus, will amplify the severe 
threat in the eastern CWA during the afternoon before activity 
rapidly exits the area in the evening. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Friday through Tuesday/... 
With strong dry air advection in place behind the departing trough, 
weather conditions will turn much quieter beginning Friday. A piece 
of energy left behind from departing trough is currently being 
depicted by the model guidance to separate itself from the main jet 
energy and briefly morph into a cut-off low over AZ during the 
weekend. This feature for the most part should be inconsequential, 
although enough moisture could be present for some showers to 
materialize over the AZ high terrain on Saturday but for the most 
part should remain on the light side given the overall lack of 
instability that will be present. The lower deserts should remain 
rain-free as there will be too much dry air in place. Under the 
presence of the low, temperatures will be several degrees below 
normal during the weekend with afternoon highs struggling to reach 
80 degrees across the lower deserts. As the upper-level low exits 
the region and weak ridging builds overhead early next week, 
temperatures will rebound to more seasonal levels.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0550Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
The main aviation concern through Thursday morning will be the
potential for another round of VCTS/TS which could impact the
metro terminals, result in gusty winds, brief heavy rainfall,
lightning, and hail. Currently there is a lull in thunderstorm
activity across southcentral AZ, however storm chances will ramp
up again after midnight. The most likely period of time to see
thunderstorms will be between 10Z-16Z Thursday morning. Winds will
continue out of the east through much of the overnight period.
Once thunderstorms develop, outflow will result in a NW shift
followed by a westerly shift once storms clear east of the
terminals late Thursday morning. CIGs are expected to remain
around 5-7K ft AGL overnight, however there could be a period of
CIGs as low as 3-5K as showers progress through the metro area.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No major aviation weather concerns are anticipated through the
forecast period. Winds will favor a southerly to southwesterly
component at KBLH and westerly at KIPL. Gusts up to 25 kts will
become common at both terminals early Thursday afternoon. FEW to 
SCT clouds, mostly aoa 7 kft, will prevail.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A low pressure system will bring very active weather conditions 
across much of central and eastern AZ through Thursday as multiple
rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected. Significant 
rainfall activity is likely in some areas, particularly across the 
higher terrain areas of the eastern districts where rainfall amounts 
in excess of 1-2" are possible. MinRHs through Thursday will range 
between 30-40% across the western districts and between 40-70% 
across the eastern districts along with good to excellent overnight 
recoveries. Some gusty winds with peak gusts upwards of 25-30 mph 
are likely this afternoon and once again on Thursday across the 
western districts. Much quieter conditions are expected starting 
Friday along with a decrease in humidity values. Near normal 
temperatures today will cool into a below normal category starting 
Thursday and lasting through the weekend.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Flood Watch through Thursday evening for AZZ545-547-552-556>558-
     560>563.

     Flood Watch through Thursday afternoon for AZZ534-537-538-
     540>544-546-548>551-553>555.

CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...18
LONG TERM...Lojero 
AVIATION...Salerno
FIRE WEATHER...Lojero
